✅ **Prompt Updated**: Showcase Treatment (showcase_treatment)

Updated prompt: showcase_treatment

📜 **Version 2** saved (use `action:"history"` to view)

**Changes**: +6 additions, -5 deletions

```diff
===================================================================
--- a/development/showcase_treatment/prompt.yaml
+++ b/development/showcase_treatment/prompt.yaml
@@ -1,7 +1,6 @@
 id: showcase_treatment
 name: Showcase Treatment
-description: Translate the approved silent story and references into storyboard,
-  color script, typography, logo disposition and editorial pacing.
+description: Specify the five-role palette states and the per-asset contract (roles, shadow shapes, boil variants, reference) for the settled style.
 category: development
 systemMessageFile: system-message.md
 userMessageTemplateFile: user-message.md
===================================================================
--- a/development/showcase_treatment/user-message.md
+++ b/development/showcase_treatment/user-message.md
@@ -4,8 +4,10 @@
 Previous handoff:
 {{context | default("Read available chain history; report missing evidence.")}}
 
-Translate the story into a coherent outward-facing visual treatment. Retrieve and inspect the existing README, logo and related assets before proposing evolution. Use observed properties rather than borrowed labels. The planner decides the selected direction and whether a logo evolution is earned; preserve the current mark until that ruling exists.
+Read, before writing, the project files under the production root's `v3/`: `creative-spec.md` (rulings D41–D53, medium, palette law, animation language), `script.md` (resource vocabulary and beats), `rubric.md` (criteria C1–C18 and the receipt shape). They are the contract; this prompt does not restate them.
 
-Deliver treatment.md and a storyboard when paths are owned. Specify a one-line visual law, compositional grammar, typography roles, contrast/readability expectations and a beat-addressed color script (ground, information, actor, state and payoff roles). Connect color changes to story state. Define scene hierarchy, artifact hero framing and editorial pacing/holds; identify the small number of frames the planner must inspect. Include references with observed/interpretation/transfer separation, a useful boundary/counterexample and the before/after rationale for any brand evolution. Keep actual output and evidence markers readable.
+Translate the script into the asset and palette contract, not a mood. The style is settled (D44, D48, D50): flat five-role assets on a black field, Seuss contour architecture, Midnight Gospel stipple shadows, radiance as the only light. Do not propose a new look; specify what each beat needs in it.
 
-Return: Visual Law; References; Storyboard; Color Script; Typography and Brand; Editorial Pacing; Artifact Handoff; Concerns. Hand complete beat-addressed instructions to the motion designer.
\ No newline at end of file
+Deliver under the production root: (1) `tokens` values for the three states (settled, overwhelm, scaffold) as role maps per asset family, sampled from the filed references in `v3/references/` and named by source; identity pigments (Codex blue/cyan, Clawd coral/dark) are listed once and never graded; (2) an asset list, one row per object the script names, with its five role slots, its form-shadow and cast-shadow shapes, its boil variants (2–3), and the reference whose contour language it borrows; (3) the frames the planner must inspect, by beat, and what each must show. Hex values appear only in the tokens file; an asset that carries a hex literal fails C2.
+
+Return: Palette States; Asset Contract; Shadow Law per Asset; Inspection Frames; Artifact Handoff; Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file

```
